description: Fetch clinical trial results data from ClinicalTrials.gov for completed studies — outcome measures with statistics, adverse events, participant flow, baseline characteristics, and results metadata (limitations & caveats, certain-agreement disclosure restrictions, results point of contact). Posted results exist only for studies where hasResults is true; the entry for a study without them names, in resultPublications, the journal articles its record lists as reporting its results (RESULT references, with PMID and citation), when it lists any. Use clinicaltrials_search_studies first to find studies with results. Each call fetches up to 20 distinct NCT IDs and returns any further IDs in deferredNctIds for a follow-up call. A results-rich record can exceed 500KB per study in full mode — bound it with summary=true, narrower sections, or the outcomeLimit / adverseEventLimit caps; outcomeLimit / outcomeOffset also page summarized outcomes. A bounded list is resumable: outcomeOffset / seriousEventOffset / otherEventOffset start the next window, and each study's filtersApplied reports what was trimmed and the next offset for every list left short. A previous (alias) NCT ID resolves to its canonical study, named in canonicalNctId.

adverseEventLimit.description: Optional cap on the number of serious and other adverse events returned per study, applied to each list separately in upstream order. Omit for no cap (every event); a limit at or past a list’s length returns that whole list. Applies to full mode only — summary mode already ranks the top 20 by the most participants affected in any one event group. Event groups are never capped. Upstream totals preserved in filtersApplied.totalSeriousEvents / totalOtherEvents only when the cap trims a list.

anyOf.description: Multiple NCT IDs, at most 500 entries counting repeats.

nctIds.description: One or more NCT IDs — an empty list is rejected, and a repeated ID collapses to one results entry in first-occurrence order. A call fetches the first 20 distinct IDs; any further distinct IDs come back unfetched in deferredNctIds, in first-occurrence order, for a follow-up call. A list over 500 entries, repeats included, is rejected. E.g., "NCT12345678" or ["NCT12345678", "NCT87654321"]. Use summary=true for large batches to avoid large payloads.

otherEventOffset.description: Optional index of the first other (non-serious) adverse event to return, in upstream order. Omit or 0 to start at the first. Pages independently of seriousEventOffset and pairs with adverseEventLimit. Continue from filtersApplied.nextOtherEventOffset until that field is absent. Applied to every study in the call. Rejected with summary: true or when sections excludes adverseEvents.

outcomeLimit.description: Optional cap on the number of outcome measures returned per study, taken in the order ClinicalTrials.gov publishes them. Omit for no cap (every measure); a limit at or past the list length returns the whole list. Applies in both modes: each surviving measure keeps its complete groups/classes/measurements/analyses tree in full mode, or its whole summary projection with summary: true. Upstream total preserved in filtersApplied.totalOutcomes only when the cap trims the list.

outcomeOffset.description: Optional index of the first outcome measure to return, in the order ClinicalTrials.gov publishes them. Omit or 0 to start at the first. Pair with outcomeLimit to page a long list: each response reports filtersApplied.nextOutcomeOffset for the study, and the list is exhausted when that field is absent. Applied to every study in the call. An offset at or past the end returns an empty list with filtersApplied.totalOutcomes stating the upstream length, not an error. Works in summary mode too, paging the summarized measures. Rejected when sections excludes outcomes.

sections.description: Filter which sections to return. Values: outcomes, adverseEvents, participantFlow, baseline, moreInfo. Omit for all sections — an empty list is rejected, not treated as omission.

seriousEventOffset.description: Optional index of the first serious adverse event to return, in upstream order. Omit or 0 to start at the first. Pages independently of otherEventOffset — the two lists have uncorrelated lengths — and pairs with adverseEventLimit, which bounds each list separately. Continue from filtersApplied.nextSeriousEventOffset until that field is absent. Applied to every study in the call. Rejected with summary: true or when sections excludes adverseEvents.

summary.description: Return condensed summaries instead of full data. Full mode renders every row and field on both output channels, so a large results set can exceed 500KB per study; summary mode typically cuts that to a few KB, scaling with the measure count and the participant flow’s groups × periods rather than to a fixed ceiling. An outcome summary keeps the title, type, timeframe, paramType, dispersionType, unit, group/class/analysis counts, per-group denominators, a top-line projection of a single class/category cell — labelled with the class and category titles it came from, that class’s own denominators, and a count of the siblings it omits — and the first statistical analysis with its group description and compared groups named by title. The measurements outside that cell and the remaining analyses are dropped; re-run with summary=false to reach them. An adverse-event summary keeps each event group’s death, serious, and other totals beside the ranked topEvents; a participant-flow summary keeps the group roster and every period’s milestones with per-group counts, leaving milestone comments and drop/withdraw reasons to full mode. outcomeLimit / outcomeOffset page the summarized outcome list as they page full mode; the adverse-event bounds do not apply here, since topEvents ranks the whole event list. For a middle ground, keep full mode and cap the two lists that carry the bulk with outcomeLimit / adverseEventLimit.

name: clinicaltrials_get_study_results

deferredNctIds.description: Requested NCT IDs past the per-call cap of 20 distinct IDs, normalized and deduplicated, in first-occurrence order. Not fetched — pass them as nctIds in a follow-up call. Absent when every requested ID was processed.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `blank_value`: A parameter was supplied with a blank, whitespace-only, or empty-list value. `offset_not_applicable`: An offset was supplied for a list this call does not return as a window — an adverse-event offset in summary mode, which ranks the whole event list into topEvents, or any offset whose own section the sections filter excludes. `rate_limited`: ClinicalTrials.gov answered HTTP 429 on every attempt, or the call’s time budget ran out after a 429. `retry_deadline_exceeded`: ClinicalTrials.gov did not answer within the call’s time budget, which covers every request, retry, and wait the call makes — the batch and any per-ID fetches share it. `upstream_timeout`: ClinicalTrials.gov answered HTTP 504 (gateway timeout) or 408 (request timeout), or sent no answer within the per-attempt timeout, on every attempt of the batch request or of a per-ID fetch. `upstream_unavailable`: Every attempt of the batch request or of a per-ID fetch failed on ClinicalTrials.gov’s side — HTTP 500, 502, or 503, a dropped connection or one the network gave up opening, or a 200 body that is not the JSON the route serves (an HTML page, unparseable text, the wrong shape) — or it answered that request with another 5xx, such as 505, or the connection was refused or its host name did not resolve, none of which is retried. `upstream_rejected`: ClinicalTrials.gov refused the batch request or a per-ID fetch with a status its API does not use for a bad query — HTTP 501, a 3xx, or a 4xx such as 401, 403, or 410 — or answered it with an HTML error page in place of its own 404. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

fetchErrors.description: Requested NCT IDs with no study on ClinicalTrials.gov: absent from the batch answer, or refused as not found when fetched one by one. Any other failure ends the call with its own error and never lands here.

adverseEvents.description: Adverse events. Summary mode: timeFrame, frequencyThreshold, groupCount, seriousEventCount, otherEventCount, eventGroups (each event group’s id, title, and whole-study totals — deathsNumAffected / deathsNumAtRisk, seriousNumAffected / seriousNumAtRisk, otherNumAffected / otherNumAtRisk — as upstream sends them; a total the study does not publish is absent, not 0), plus topEvents — up to 20 events ranked by the most participants affected in any one event group, each with term, organSystem, kind, and byGroup (one { groupId, numAffected, numAtRisk } row per event group; resolve groupId against eventGroups). Counts are never pooled across groups: groups can overlap (a crossover or second-course group re-counts participants of its parent arm), so compare arms row by row. Full mode: frequencyThreshold, eventGroups with descriptions and per-group totals, plus seriousEvents and otherEvents with per-event term and per-group affected/at-risk stats. frequencyThreshold, in either mode, is the reporting threshold as upstream sends it: other (non-serious) events are listed only when their frequency reaches it, so an other event the study does not list may still have occurred below it. Usually a percentage ("5", "0"), occasionally text ("any"); absent when the study publishes none.

baseline.description: Baseline characteristics. Summary mode: groupCount, measureCount, and measures (title, paramType, unitOfMeasure). Full mode: adds groups and measures with per-group classes/categories/measurements.

canonicalNctId.description: The canonical NCT identifier of the study that answered — present only when the requested nctId is a previous (alias) ID pointing at a different record. Absent means nctId is already canonical. Requesting an alias and its own canonical ID together returns one entry per requested ID, both carrying the same study.

filtersApplied.description: What the outcomeLimit / adverseEventLimit caps and the outcomeOffset / seriousEventOffset / otherEventOffset offsets trimmed on this study, plus the next offset for each list left short. In summary mode only the outcome bounds apply. Present only when a bound actually reduced a list — a window that started at zero and reached the end trimmed nothing. Absent means the payload is the complete upstream set for the requested sections. Offsets apply uniformly to every study in the call, so continuation is reported per study: each exhausts its lists at a different index.

adverseEventLimit.description: Echo of the adverseEventLimit input — present only when the cap cut events off the end of a window. Which list it cut is named by that list’s own next offset.

nextOtherEventOffset.description: The otherEventOffset to request next for this study — present only when other events remain past the window. Absent means this study’s other event list is exhausted.

nextOutcomeOffset.description: The outcomeOffset to request next for this study — present only when measures remain past the window. Absent means this study’s outcome list is exhausted.

nextSeriousEventOffset.description: The seriousEventOffset to request next for this study — present only when serious events remain past the window. Absent means this study’s serious event list is exhausted.

otherEventOffset.description: Echo of the otherEventOffset input — present only when it skipped events before the window.

outcomeLimit.description: Echo of the outcomeLimit input — present only when the cap cut measures off the end of the window.

outcomeOffset.description: Echo of the outcomeOffset input — present only when it skipped measures before the window.

seriousEventOffset.description: Echo of the seriousEventOffset input — present only when it skipped events before the window.

totalOtherEvents.description: Upstream other adverse event count, before the bounds trimmed the list.

totalOutcomes.description: Upstream outcome measure count, before the bounds trimmed the list.

totalSeriousEvents.description: Upstream serious adverse event count, before the bounds trimmed the list.

moreInfo.description: Results metadata from moreInfoModule. Summary mode: limitationsAndCaveats, certainAgreement flags (piSponsorEmployee, restrictiveAgreement, restrictionType), and pointOfContact. Full mode: adds certainAgreement.otherDetails.

nctId.description: The NCT identifier as requested, trimmed and uppercased. When it is a previous (alias) ID, ClinicalTrials.gov answers with the canonical record and canonicalNctId names it.

outcomes.description: Outcome measures with per-group statistics. Summary mode (compact): type, title, timeFrame, paramType, dispersionType, unitOfMeasure, groupCount / classCount, analysisCount (how many analyses the measure carries, when it has any), denoms (the whole measure’s per-group denominators keyed by group title), topStats (the per-group cells of one class/category — each carrying the upstream value verbatim, including an NA/NR sentinel, plus spread, lowerLimit/upperLimit, and the record’s own comment when present), topStatsFrom (classTitle / categoryTitle naming where that cell came from, classDenoms — that class’s own denominators, shaped like denoms, when upstream publishes them — omittedClasses / omittedCategories counts, and a note pointing at summary=false when siblings were dropped), and topAnalysis (statisticalMethod, pValue, paramType/Value, ciPctValue/Lower/Upper, nonInferiorityType, groupDescription naming the subgroup or comparison, groupIds, and groups — the compared groups’ titles in groupIds order — lifted from analyses[0]) when present. Every summary field is resolved per measure. Full mode (default): adds raw groups, classes, categories, measurements, and analyses arrays.

participantFlow.description: Participant flow milestones and drop-outs. Summary mode: groupCount, periodCount, groups (id and title of each flow group), and periods — each with its title and every milestone in upstream order as { type, achievements: [{ groupId, numSubjects }] }, numSubjects verbatim as upstream sends it (a string); resolve groupId against groups. Full mode: the whole module — adds recruitment and pre-assignment details, group descriptions, milestone and achievement comments, numUnits, and each period’s dropWithdraws.

resultPublications.description: Journal articles the study record lists as reporting its results (its references of type RESULT), in registry order and uncapped — present only when hasResults is false and the record lists at least one. BACKGROUND and DERIVED references are not included; clinicaltrials_get_study_record lists every reference.

items.description: One RESULT reference of the study record.

citation.description: The citation as the record gives it.

pmid.description: PubMed ID of the article — absent when the record lists none.

retractions.description: Retraction notices the record links to the article — absent when it has none.

items.description: One retraction notice for the article.

pmid.description: PubMed ID of the retraction notice.

source.description: Where the retraction notice was published.

studiesWithoutResults.description: NCT IDs of the studies with no results posted to ClinicalTrials.gov. Each still has its entry in results, carrying resultPublications when its record lists any.

truncated.description: True when a bound — a cap or an offset — trimmed a list on at least one study; absent when nothing was trimmed, matching filtersApplied one level down. Which study, which list, and where to resume is named in that study’s filtersApplied.

title: Clinicaltrials Get Study Results
